signature.name: One Lead Mover
signature.description: At every moment exactly one element carries 'working on it', and every other moving part is visibly quieter, nearby, and on a tempo that nests with the lead rather than competing with it.

lesson: The strong loaders are the ones where one thing moves and everything else breathes; the weak ones keep a second idea (a counter, a hitch, a reset) that the waiting eye has to track.

bare-wire.signature_why: One dark hole at a time is the clear lead; the 5s field bloom and the 2.5s glint nest under it, and the reduced-motion version keeps a single breathing scar as the focal point. The two drops land about 11 units apart, which nudges the eye slightly.
bare-wire.loved: The wound now closes instead of a second ring spreading: it opens in 0.3s, holds, then sinks away over 1.7s at 0.4Hz, and the 120px frame reads as a real hole in crema.
bare-wire.docked: Two landings per 5s still reads as a gentle pulse, and the bare field at each handoff is a tiny dead beat; the pasted second SVG is still duplicated markup.
bare-wire.fix_note: The 1Hz target pulse is gone and the cap holds (.55 at that offset clears the cup wall, which was what I wanted). They overruled #8A5A33 with #6B4226 for contrast, which is a fair call. They rejected one-per-5s in favour of two per loop for a felt beat, and that reason mostly holds.

warm-hands.signature_why: The linear sweep is the only real mover; the static stream only shimmers in opacity and lands at the centre, and the bloom breathes underneath it on the same 5s clock. My eye goes to the spiral every time at both sizes, and reduced motion holds the stream and spiral as one focal pose.
warm-hands.loved: The thin stream turns 'a spiral that spins' into 'a spiral being poured' in one glance at 120px, without touching the seamless sweep and sway.
warm-hands.docked: At 120px the spiral is still the biggest shape and still a turning rosette, so spinner grammar survives. The stream is faint where it crosses paper above the rim, and the stain ring is still busy at in-app size.
warm-hands.fix_note: They built the stream as I specified (3 units, outside .sweep, opacity-only 5s shimmer, held under reduced motion). They also thickened the stain to 3.6 and made it static, a sensible partial take on the stain half of my note. The stream ends at the spiral's origin (54,57), which orbits the 54,60 pivot by 3 units, so you can barely see it move.

the-glitch.signature_why: The 1s drop leads and everything stays in one column, which is good. But the crema count (opacity .10 to .80) is the largest contrast change in the loop and competes with the drop. Its 0.25s drain at 4.75s, plus the 3.0-3.5s pull, give the eye two more events to track.
the-glitch.loved: Without the orange layer, the gravity-eased drop now fades in at the spout and squashes into its ring with no hard cuts, and it is the most literal coffee ritual on the table.
the-glitch.docked: The pip counter that reset every loop has moved into the coffee: the cup climbs to a near-full crema at 4.6s and then drains in 0.25s. That is a fill and reset, the fake-finish grammar I asked them to remove. The pull adds a scheduled hitch near 3s.
the-glitch.fix_note: The orange pips, slip and ghost are all gone, as asked. I asked for the drop and ring to be the only clock; they refused because 'a cup with no count is a glide'. That reason does not hold: the 1s drop already counts, and the new count resets just as visibly as the pips did.
